original.indicated: the marketplace entry, ci.yml, README.md, CLAUDE.md, the release notes and the mod README change; no icon file

issue.why_categorical: a repo contract the plan's file set did not cover
issue.why_free_form: tests/contract/test_plugin_icons.py requires .claude-plugin/icon.png (square PNG, 512-2048 px) for every local marketplace plugin; adding the lap-stamp marketplace entry without one fails it

new_outcome.indicated: TASK-6 also adds plugins/lap-stamp/.claude-plugin/icon.png, a 512x512 stopwatch drawn with the standard library

why_new_outcome.free_form: without the icon the marketplace entry breaks an existing contract test

original.indicated: session.append with door delivery or queue during a main turn calls delivered; register.ts is wired only in TASK-9

issue.why_categorical: the plan misread the host door set, and a host load rule the plan did not know blocks the item's own tests
issue.why_free_form: The host typings (SessionAppendDoor) define door queue as the message-queue record raised when a prompt is queued at Enter, not a delivery into the running turn; treating it as one restarts the running turn's lap on every mid-turn press, against D2. Separately, the host refuses every $ call a hook makes unless the plugin's scanned hooks module (register.ts) calls it, so lap.test.ts cannot pass while register.ts is the TASK-1 stub.

new_outcome.indicated: Only door delivery (main loop, lap-press origin) calls delivered; a queue row leaves the press pending for the next turn. TASK-7 also wires register.ts to registerLap; TASK-9 adds registerRender to it.

why_new_outcome.free_form: D2 anchors a mid-turn press to the running turn only on a reported delivery; the register.ts wiring is an execution blocker for the item's planned tests

issue.why_categorical: the planned hook order loses the press for the turn it starts
issue.why_free_form: The turn a lap press starts begins inside next, so a prompt.submit hook that awaited next first would queue the press after turn.start had already looked for it; that turn would time from the wrong start and the press would wait for the following turn.

new_outcome.indicated: prompt.submit takes the press before next so the turn that starts inside next finds it, and withdraws it when next returns a drop; every other hook awaits next first.

why_new_outcome.free_form: D1 times a turn from its press; only a press queued before next is visible to the turn that starts inside it, and the withdrawal keeps a dropped prompt from leaving a stale press.

original.indicated: test_the_release_notes_list_the_mod reads the notes file named by the marketplace metadata.version; test_claude_md_names_and_counts_the_mod pins the literal 'ten TypeScript mods'

issue.why_categorical: the planned test reached its file by a path built at runtime and pinned a count another test owns
issue.why_free_form: tools/select_tests.py cannot see a release-notes file named from metadata.version, so a pull request touching the notes skips the check, and the check fails once the next release bumps the version; the mod count is already checked by tests/contract/test_mod_count.py and the literal pin breaks when the next mod lands

new_outcome.indicated: The committed test declares WALK_ROOTS = ('docs/RELEASES/',), collects the lap-stamp rows across docs/RELEASES/v*.md and requires one ending in the manifest version, following test_arc_straps_registration.py; the CLAUDE.md test keeps the name and mirror-test assertions and drops the count pin. The planned copy under docs/plans/2031/tests stays as frozen.

why_new_outcome.free_form: CLAUDE.md requires a walking test to declare WALK_ROOTS so PR selection reaches it, and the mod count has one owner

changes.discovered_by: developer request after the first live turn (TASK-10)

original.indicated: render returns the original tree with dim, right-aligned Text rows under it; the TurnDuration stamp is dim Text on the same row

issue.why_categorical: the developer asked for a colored stamp after seeing it live
issue.why_free_form: The developer asked for the lap timer in oxblood, maroon, dark orange or similar. Dim text reads as part of the engine's own chrome; a color sets the stamp apart. Pure maroon (#800000) nearly vanishes on a dark terminal background, so the color sits between oxblood and dark orange.

new_outcome.indicated: Both stamp sites draw Text with color STAMP_COLOR = '#B7410E' (rust), exported from hooks/render.tsx, instead of dimColor; the render and register tests select stamp rows by that color; the mod README names it.

why_new_outcome.free_form: a colored stamp is told apart from the engine's dim lines at a glance

changes.discovered_by: developer request after the first live turns

original.indicated: the glue writes rows and holds them for render; nothing reads the laps file back for the developer

issue.why_categorical: the developer asked to read the recorded timings as a table
issue.why_free_form: The rows were only readable as raw JSONL. The developer asked for /lap-times: a markdown table of the laps capped at the current terminal width, with cleaner formatting than the /todo table (whose cells are not padded, so its columns wander as plain text). A skill run through the model cannot learn the terminal width (the Bash tool sees no COLUMNS); a mod command's command.run carries presentation.columns.

new_outcome.indicated: lap.ts registers /lap-times [all] [N] at session.start in an active project and answers command.run without a model turn (isTextDisplayOnly); hooks/table.ts renders the summary line and a padded markdown table that drops columns least useful first to fit presentation.columns (stop time and lap always kept); row.ts adds parseAllRows for the all-sessions view.

why_new_outcome.free_form: the recorded timings become readable in the terminal on demand
